subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and what exact activity source, thresholds, nudge content, kill semantics, parent wake contract, and channel-visible notification behavior should it use?
rationale: The remaining work adds new recovery policy, config/default behavior, mutating child-run control, and user-visible channel failure handling, so automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Define core recovery policy
options.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge/kill behavior, parent wakeup, channel notification wording, and relationship to session activity and kill/reap work.

options.title: Prototype default-off
options.body: Allow an experimental opt-in watchdog first, with focused live proof and no behavior change for existing installs until maintainers accept defaults.

options.title: Defer automatic recovery
options.body: Rely on runTimeoutSeconds and future manual kill/reap controls for now, then revisit automatic nudge/kill after more production evidence or session-activity infrastructure lands.

recommendation.title: Define core recovery policy
recommendation.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge/kill behavior, parent wakeup, channel notification wording, and relationship to session activity and kill/reap work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the subagent registry/control boundary and adjacent timeout semantics.
